name: Tarshish
overview: Tarshish was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Bilhan. His mention is brief and focused solely on his lineage within the tribe, without additional notes or events recorded. This positions him as a minor yet distinct figure within the genealogical records of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Tarshish is a proper name whose meanings possibly include 'yellow jasper,' 'greedy one,' or relate to a 'foundry' or 'refinery.' These meanings provide insight into the possible symbolic or occupational significance of the name, though the name itself was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Tarshish as the son of Bilhan, linking him directly to his father within the tribe of Benjamin. Beyond this paternal connection, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Tarshish's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical record of the tribe of Benjamin, serving as a link in the lineage that God preserved among His chosen people. While not a prominent figure in narrative events, his inclusion emphasizes the faithfulness of God in maintaining the heritage of Israel's tribes. This genealogical mention underlines the importance of every individual in the unfolding of God's redemptive plan through the nation of Israel.
